profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This CoreSite facility is in one of the company confirmed operating markets. Wikipedia coverage states that as of June 2022 CoreSite operated 27 data center facilities across 10 markets totaling over 4.6 million net rentable square feet, with key locations including Boston, Chicago, Denver, Los Angeles, Miami, New York City, Northern Virginia, San Francisco/San Jose, Santa Clara, Atlanta, Orlando, and Washington, D.C. In May 2007 the company acquired Chicago properties as part of a wider expansion. CoreSite began operating a Washington, D.C. facility in August 2005, one of its earliest East Coast sites after founding in 2001 as CRG West. CoreSite rebranded from CRG West to CoreSite in June 2009, went public in September 2010, and was acquired by American Tower in December 2021. This specific market was confirmed as an active CoreSite location, but no market specific acquisition date or building history beyond the general company timeline was located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
CoreSite AT2 publishes 67,000 square feet of technical space but no power figure, making it impossible to assess its contribution to AI infrastructure without assumptions the operator has not supplied.

The 67,000-square-foot footprint places AT2 in the mid-sized colocation range, suitable for enterprise workloads but not in the hyperscale category now driving AI compute deployment. Without a megawatt figure, the square footage alone cannot translate to racks, GPU density, or AI training capacity. That gap matters because power density varies by workload and cooling design, and the operator chose not to publish either.

The facility holds six compliance certifications spanning financial services, payment processing, health data, information security, and federal security standards. These qualifications serve regulated enterprises and their data but do not signal readiness for large-scale AI training. AI infrastructure specifications like power redundancy tier, cooling architecture, and GPU-to-rack configuration are absent from the published profile.

Georgia's index shows 33 facilities statewide, but only 2 publish megawatt figures, totaling 42 MW combined. AT2's missing power data means Georgia appears as a thin compute picture for AI, and whether AT2 adds materially to that figure remains unknown. For readers tracking grid constraints on AI scaling, a state where the largest facilities hide their power consumption is a state that has not yet made its capacity visible to the market.
